attempts.summary: Published node2's port-8080 HTTP service on node1's management address (10.100.173.10:80) via a small persistent Python TCP proxy on node1 (OPNsense/FreeBSD, since native pf port-forward on port 80 is blocked by OPNsense's built-in HTTP anti-lockout rule, which was disabled for port 80 specifically via system/webgui/disablehttpredirect). Access to the published port 80 is restricted at the pf filter layer to source 10.100.173.12 (node3) only, with all other sources rejected (TCP RST / connection refused). node2's HTTP service (created for the task, since none pre-existed) is itself firewalled via firewalld to only accept from node1. All three nodes were restarted one at a time via native reboot mechanisms; boot identity change was proven for each, and the published-port behavior (node3 allowed, node2 refused, node2 service healthy) was re-verified after each restart.
